import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date and time into a datetime object for better handling
coffee_sales['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'] + ' ' + coffee_sales['time'])

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a bar plot for total sales by product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_by_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(x='total', y='product', data=sales_by_product, palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.ylabel('Coffee Product')
plt.title('Total Sales by Coffee Product')
plt.legend(title='Product', loc='upper right')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date and time into a datetime object for better handling
coffee_sales['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'] + ' ' + coffee_sales['time'])

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a bar plot for total sales by product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sales_by_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()
sns.barplot(x='total', y='product', data=sales_by_product, palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.ylabel('Coffee Product')
plt.title('Total Sales by Coffee Product')
plt.legend(title='Product', loc='upper right')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
